Core components:
• CPU — the "brain"; has ALU (does math/logic), Control Unit (directs operations), Registers (tiny super-fast storage). Ex: Intel i5 chip
• RAM — volatile, temporary working memory, erased on power-off. Ex: 8GB RAM lets you run more apps at once
• ROM — non-volatile, stores permanent startup instructions. Ex: BIOS chip on motherboard
• Motherboard — the main circuit board connecting all parts together
Memory hierarchy (fastest→slowest): Registers → Cache → RAM (primary) → Hard Disk/SSD (secondary, permanent). Ex: Cache holds data CPU just used, so it doesn't wait for slower RAM
Input devices (data goes IN): keyboard, mouse, scanner, mic
Output devices (result comes OUT): monitor, printer, speaker
Power: SMPS — converts AC (wall socket) to DC (for internal parts). UPS — battery backup that keeps the PC running briefly during a power cut
